items.title: Live: Refinery hit by major blaze says fuel production secure, gas leak under investigation
items.description: Energy Minister Chris Bowen says the facility is still producing diesel and jet fuel but "at reduced levels, as a precaution". Follow live.

items.title: Live: Australia secures additional diesel shipments as Trump rules out extending ceasefire
items.description: US President Donald Trump says a long-term peace deal with Iran is "preferable" and to expect an "amazing two days" ahead. Follow live.

items.title: Australian dollar surges to four-year high as traders see end to Iran war
items.description: Analysts say the mood on global financial markets has improved considerably over the past few days.

items.title: Live: Marles says $53b defence plan strengthens 'self-reliance'
items.description: Richard Marles says the new plan, the National Defence Strategy 2026,  affirms that Australia is facing its "most complex and threatening strategic circumstances since the end of World War II". Follow live.

items.title: Is LIV Golf dead? Not yet, but the vultures are circling
items.description: Rumours of LIV Golf's immediate demise look wide of the mark, but the smoke is only growing thicker as denials from the league's CEO help paint a bleak picture.

items.title: Prince Harry to headline mental health summit on day three of Australian visit
items.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are back together in Melbourne after spending the second day of their Australian tour apart.

items.title: Controversial laws to restrict protests in NSW struck down by top court
items.description: The laws, rushed through parliament after the Bondi Beach terrorist attack, have been found to be unconstitutional by the state's highest court.

items.title: New data reveals age group spending up big
items.description: Australians spent more in March as the outbreak of the Iran war drove up petrol prices. Older Australians increased their spending at the fastest pace, CBA data shows.

items.title: Why Australia turned to tiny nation to secure critical fertiliser supplies
items.description: The Middle East conflict has disrupted the flow of Australia's imports of the fertiliser urea. Facing the potential threat of reduced crop yields, Anthony Albanese looked to Australia's neighbours.

items.title: Unemployment rate remains at 4.3pc in 'calm before the storm'
items.description: Australia's unemployment rate remained at 4.3 per cent in March, but economists say cracks could start appearing in coming months.

items.title: Uncovered ballots prompt new count in key SA seat won by One Nation
items.description: The Electoral Commission of South Australia has uncovered more than 600 ballot papers that were not counted in the recent state election, including dozens from the closely contested seat of Narungga on the Yorke Peninsula.

items.title: Underworld figure had 'never' sat outside at cafe until day he was shot, court told
items.description: Victoria's Supreme Court is told underworld figure Gavin Preston was cautious about his surroundings and "never" sat outside a cafe he regularly attended — other than the day he was shot dead.

items.title: Liberty Bell Bay workers told to take leave without pay or be sacked
items.description: About 175 workers at Australia's only manganese smelter, Liberty Bell Bay, have been told they will be laid off at the end of next week unless they take leave without pay.

items.title: Rebel Wilson's The Deb is a delight despite the ongoing legal drama
items.description: Plus a powerful look Palestinian life through multiple generations and a buzzy Japanese video game adaptation makes it to Australian shores.

items.title: Quiz: Can you tell the difference between The Pitt and ER?
items.description: Ahead of The Pitt season finale dropping this week, can you pick the difference between it and its hospital drama ancestor ER?

items.title: How this tiny town welcomed a 70-piece orchestra
items.description: The Sydney Youth Orchestras travelled to this tiny town to help inspire the local kids, but when they left, they were the ones who felt changed.

items.title: Video shows father and son illegally scuttling boat off NSW South Coast
items.description: In a historic judgment, the two fishermen are fined $15,000 for towing their vessel out to sea and illegally scuttling it.

items.title: Live: Unemployment remains at 4.3pc, Viva Energy in trading halt after fire
items.description: Viva Energy is in a trading halt after a fire at its Geelong oil refinery. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Russian missiles hit Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, 12 dead
items.description: Russian forces have attacked the Ukrainian capital Kyiv and other cities, killing 12 people, as the defence leaders of more than 50 countries say they are aiming to send more aid to Ukraine.

items.title: Man, 53, charged over seizure of more than 350 cannabis plants
items.description: A 53-year-old Kalgoorlie man is released on bail after the seizure of more than 350 cannabis plants from a property WA Police allege had been converted for the purpose of growing hydroponic cannabis.

items.title: Former Launceston mayor resigns from council after scandal-plagued term
items.description: The former mayor and councillor of Tasmanian's second-largest city resigns effective immediately, years after an ABC investigation uncovered historical allegations about his conduct towards young men in the theatre scene.

items.title: Smoky Sydney as 5,000 hectares burned in hazard reduction blitz
items.description: Smoky conditions across Greater Sydney are tipped to ease tomorrow as the wind picks up, after firefighters had a productive week burning hazards around Sydney's fringes.

items.title: Pandemic, 'ice epidemic' worsened Qld child safety pressures, ex-minister says
items.description: An inquiry into Queensland's child safety system hears the former minister was made aware of the sector's resource issues, as well as the "significant increase" in children entering residential care.

items.title: Arrest warrant issued in legal battle for $27k in unpaid long service leave
items.description: It's now been over three years since two women left their jobs at a small business. Two courts later, they want their combined $27,000 in long service leave paid out to them, and say they won't give up until they get it.

items.title: Soldier protest prompts review of recruitment in PNG defence force
items.description: A small group of officers deserted their posts this week in protest over alleged government corruption.
